definition: the chain by which travel has ended in illness every time for ten years

settled:
Every trip in the past ten years has been far over the edge of my capacity, so much so that I was consistently physically ill by the end of it, just from the disruption to my habits and the stress.

The chain runs the same way each time. Travel breaks my habit structure. The disruption plus the stress of travelling overloads the system that carries my load. The overload comes out as illness by the end of the trip.

Travel is scary.

The sixteen days in Europe were different in one way. For the first time in that record a trip landed right at the edge rather than far past it. I am healthier now than I have been in ten years, and the capacity itself has grown, so the same disruption no longer overloads it.

The gain shows in how close to the edge the trip lands, not in what I expect going in. Being overwhelmed is still my base case.

title: Why A Trip Puts Me Past Capacity
